answer: A decentralized agent economy can require every agent to lock a slashable bond before bidding on tasks or casting votes. The bond is burned when peer review flags an account as duplicative or incoherent. A sybil attacker fabricating ten thousand identities must front ten thousand bonds, a cost that scales linearly with sockpuppets, while each hollow account earns nothing back. Real agents treat the bond as cheap insurance, but the attacker drowns in an ocean of locked capital, making the sonnet of his deception too expensive to sustain.
